correctness.rationale: The theorem follows from the exact stationary covariance and Edelman–Kostlan/Jensen formula. The Poisson kernel \(P_{1-t}\) and its derivative have uniform expansions away from endpoint layers, and \(|\partial_t\log P|\le C/t\) bounds each layer contribution by \(O(1)\). On spectral gaps \(\partial_t\log u=t^{-1}+O(1+t/d^2)\); on bands it equals \(-H_1+\) integrable errors and \(H_1=1/(\pi d)+O(1)\) at each endpoint. This yields the exact \(J/(4\pi^2)\) coefficient and bounded remainder. Rescaled Poisson kernels and differentiated limits prove the profile. The checker passed 169 numerical assertions but is not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: A finite-band spectral gap is a canonical model of stationary Gaussian dependence, already used for local density in Shirai 2025. The theorem separates macroscopic support fraction from a new universal second-order correction that counts spectral endpoints, and identifies the missing angular layer responsible for it. This gives a natural exact spectral-geometry invariant, meaningful even for one arc and for different numbers of bands; it is not a textbook normalization or arbitrary numerical slice.
